note: Plain-English summaries written for a repair/MSP technician and their clients. Each item links to the official source. Courses link to Microsoft Learn's live catalog pages, which Microsoft keeps current, so the link stays accurate even as the catalogue changes.

updates.title: Windows 10 is end of support - but Microsoft 365 Apps keep getting security updates until Oct 2028
updates.tldr: Windows 10 stopped getting free updates on 14 Oct 2025. Microsoft 365 Apps (the desktop Office apps) will still get SECURITY updates on Windows 10 until 10 Oct 2028, but no new features. The OS itself is the exposure, not Office.
updates.action: Plan Windows 11 upgrades or ESU. Don't let a client think their Office is unsupported - it isn't yet; the risk is the operating system underneath.

updates.title: Admins can build custom Copilot connectors (MCP) and push them org-wide
updates.tldr: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can now wire Copilot into custom/line-of-business data sources using MCP-based connectors and deploy them to the whole organisation. Previously this was limited.
updates.action: If a client asks why Copilot can't see their internal data, this is now the supported route. Treat any new data connection as a security review.

updates.title: Admins can restrict which external sites Copilot uses for web answers
updates.tldr: Domain exclusion lets an admin limit which external websites Copilot is allowed to read when it grounds answers on the web, and manage which internal sources it treats as authoritative. A privacy/data-governance control.
updates.action: Worth flagging to any client nervous about where Copilot gets its information.

updates.title: New License Requests page in the admin center
updates.tldr: Admins get a dedicated page to see, review and approve users' requests for Microsoft 365 Copilot licences, instead of chasing them manually.
updates.action: Handy to know when helping a client decide who actually needs a paid Copilot seat.

updates.title: Tools to govern Copilot agents (Agent Store review, bulk install, cost dashboard)
updates.tldr: Microsoft added admin controls around Copilot 'agents': submit in-house agents to the Agent Store after admin approval, bulk-install first-party agents, reassign ownerless ones, and track AI spend in a Cost Management dashboard.
updates.who: Larger clients rolling out Copilot agents
updates.action: Mostly relevant if a client is going deep on Copilot. Point them at their admin center if costs are a worry.

updates.title: 'New Outlook' for Windows is replacing the old Mail & Calendar apps
updates.tldr: Microsoft is moving everyone to the new Outlook app. It looks and behaves differently, stores some settings in the cloud, and a few classic features are still catching up. Clients WILL notice the change and may ask you about it.
updates.action: Know the toggle between classic and new Outlook. Reassure clients it's a Microsoft change, not a fault.

updates.title: Microsoft 365 Personal & Family prices rose when Copilot was added in
updates.tldr: Microsoft folded Copilot features into consumer Microsoft 365 Personal and Family plans and raised the price. There is a cheaper 'classic' plan without Copilot if a client asks, but it's not advertised prominently.
updates.who: Home and family clients on Personal/Family subscriptions
updates.action: If a client is annoyed about a price rise, the classic (no-Copilot) tier exists as a downgrade option.
